ai.literal: Virtuous deed what if asked, non-killing; killing other deeds all will bring.
ai.translation: If asked what the supreme virtuous deed is, it is non-killing. The act of killing brings about all other evil deeds.
ai.modern: சிறந்த அறச்செயல் எது என்று கேட்டால், அது ஓர் உயிரையும் கொல்லாமல் இருப்பதே ஆகும். கொலை செய்வது மற்ற தீய செயல்கள் எல்லாவற்றையும் ஒருவனுக்குக் கொண்டுவரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the highest virtue as the practice of non-killing (கொல்லாமை). It contrasts this with the act of killing (கோறல்), which is identified as the root cause of all other sins. By stating that killing brings all other evil deeds (பிறவினை எல்லாம் தரும்), the poet emphasizes that violence destroys the foundation of moral life. Therefore, preserving life is the ultimate ethical action from which all other virtues flow.

ai.literal: Having shared, having eaten, many lives protecting: (by) authors of texts among those compiled, of all, (it is) the head.
ai.translation: Sharing one's food and protecting all living beings is the chief among all the virtues compiled by the authors of texts.
ai.modern: தன்னிடம் உள்ள உணவை மற்றவர்களுடன் பகிர்ந்து உண்டு, பல உயிர்களையும் பாதுகாப்பது, அறநூல்களை எழுதியவர்கள் தொகுத்துக் கூறியுள்ள அறங்கள் எல்லாவற்றிலும் முதன்மையானதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the highest virtue among all moral teachings. The phrase 'பகுத்து உண்டு' emphasizes sharing one's resources, specifically food, before consuming it. 'பல்லுயிர் ஓம்புதல்' extends this compassion to protecting the lives of all creatures. The poet declares that out of everything compiled by wise authors, this twin act of sharing and protecting life stands as the supreme or 'head' ('தலை') virtue.

ai.literal: As the one good thing is non-killing; next, its behind to follow, non-lying is good.
ai.translation: Non-killing is the single greatest good. Next to it, closely following, non-lying is good.
ai.modern: ஒப்பற்ற நல்ல அறம் உயிர்களைக் கொல்லாமையாகும். அதற்கு அடுத்தபடியாகப் பொய் சொல்லாமை நல்ல அறமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet establishes a hierarchy of virtues, placing non-killing at the absolute top. The phrase 'oṉṟāka nallatu' designates non-killing as the single, unparalleled good. Right behind it, as indicated by 'ataṉ piṉ cāra', comes the virtue of non-lying. By structuring it this way, the poet emphasizes that preserving life is the highest ethical duty, while truthfulness is the second most important virtue that closely follows it.

ai.literal: Good path that which is called what if asked, whatever even one non-killing considering way.
ai.translation: If asked what is called the good path, it is the way that resolves to avoid killing any creature whatsoever.
ai.modern: நல்ல வழி என்று சொல்லப்படுவது எது என்றால், எந்தவோர் உயிரையும் கொல்லாதிருப்பதை எண்ணிச் செயல்படும் நெறியாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate righteous path in life. The phrase 'நல்லாறு' (good path) refers to the ideal way of living. When asked what this path is, the text answers that it is the way ('நெறி') that actively considers ('சூழும்') not killing ('கொல்லாமை') any living being whatsoever ('யாதொன்றும்'). The word 'சூழும்' implies a deliberate, encompassing intention to protect life in all one's actions, rather than just a passive avoidance of harm.

ai.literal: State having feared, among those who renounced all, killing having feared, non-killing he who considers is foremost.
ai.translation: Among all those who have renounced the world out of fear for its fleeting state, the foremost is he who fears taking life and commits to non-killing.
ai.modern: வாழ்க்கையின் நிலையாமையைக் கண்டு அஞ்சிப் பற்றுகளை விட்டவர்கள் அனைவரிலும், ஓர் உயிரைக் கொலை செய்வதற்கு அஞ்சி அதைக் கொல்லாமல் இருப்பதைப் பற்றிச் சிந்திப்பவனே தலைசிறந்தவன்.
ai.explanation: This couplet evaluates the greatness of those who have renounced worldly life. While many become ascetics because they fear the unstable and painful state of earthly existence, this alone does not make them the greatest. The text declares that among all renunciants, the absolute foremost is the one who fears taking life and actively upholds the principle of non-killing. The word 'talai' literally means head, but here it signifies the chief or highest position among all virtuous people.

ai.literal: non-killing having undertaken he who conducts himself lifetime upon will not go life consuming Death
ai.translation: Death, which consumes life, will not advance upon the lifespan of one who lives by the principle of non-killing.
ai.modern: உயிர்களைக் கொல்லாமை என்னும் அறத்தை ஏற்று நடப்பவனின் வாழ்நாளின் மீது, உயிரைப் பறிக்கும் எமன் செல்ல மாட்டான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet states that Death, whose nature is to consume lives, will not shorten the lifespan of a person who strictly practices non-killing. The word 'kūṟṟu' literally means the divider, referring here to Death, the entity that separates life from the body. By choosing the path of not taking any life, a person protects their own life from being prematurely taken.

ai.literal: One's own life even if departing, let not do oneself another's sweet life removing action.
ai.translation: Even if one's own life is slipping away, one must not commit the act of taking another's sweet life.
ai.modern: தன் உயிரே உடலை விட்டுப் பிரிந்து போவதாக இருந்தாலும், தான் மற்றொருவருடைய இனிய உயிரைப் போக்கும் செயலைச் செய்யக்கூடாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet establishes non-killing as an absolute principle that holds even in life-threatening situations. The phrase 'தன்னுயிர் நீப்பினும்' presents the ultimate test, insisting that one must not kill even to save oneself. By describing the other's life as 'இன்னுயிர்' (sweet life), the poet reminds us that life is just as precious and dear to others as it is to us, making the act of destroying it entirely unjustifiable.

ai.literal: Good resulting wealth great even if, to the noble ones, having killed resulting wealth lowest.
ai.translation: Even if the resulting wealth is great and good, to the noble, wealth gained by killing is the lowest.
ai.modern: நன்மையாக வரும் செல்வம் மிகப் பெரியதாக இருந்தாலும், ஓர் உயிரைக் கொன்று வரும் செல்வத்தைச் சான்றோர் மிகக் கீழானதாகவே கருதுவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the value of wealth with the means of acquiring it. The phrase 'நன்றாகும் ஆக்கம்' refers to wealth that is considered good or brings good. The poet states that no matter how vast and beneficial such prosperity might seem, if it is obtained through taking a life ('கொன்று ஆகும் ஆக்கம்'), it is deemed the absolute worst ('கடை') by noble people. The core message is that the end never justifies the means, especially when the means involves killing.

ai.literal: People of killing actions who are, [are] people of base actions, baseness those who know in the mind.
ai.translation: In the minds of those who understand true baseness, people whose trade is killing are simply people of degraded actions.
ai.modern: தீமையின் தன்மையை ஆராய்ந்து அறியும் சான்றோர்களின் உள்ளத்தில், கொலைத் தொழிலை உடையவர்கள் இழிவான செயல்களைச் செய்பவர்களாகவே கருதப்படுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet evaluates the moral standing of those who kill. The word 'மாக்கள்' usually denotes people lacking higher discernment, which perfectly fits those who commit murder. To the wise who understand true baseness ('புன்மை தெரிவார்'), murderers are inherently seen as people of polluted, degraded actions ('புலைவினையர்'). The verse emphasizes that the act of killing permanently taints a person's character in the eyes of the wise.

ai.literal: Life from body those who removed, they say, disease with body not passing cruel life they.
ai.translation: They say that those who endure a cruel, unending life in a diseased body are the ones who once separated life from the bodies of others.
ai.modern: நோயால் துன்புறும் உடம்போடு நீங்காத கொடிய வாழ்க்கையை வாழ்பவர்கள், முன்பு பிற உயிர்களை அவற்றின் உடம்பிலிருந்து பிரித்துக் கொன்றவர்கள் என்று அறிஞர் கூறுவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet connects the act of killing to the experience of severe physical suffering. The phrase 'உயிர் உடம்பின் நீக்கியார்' directly describes killers as those who separate life from a body. The consequence is described as 'செயிர் உடம்பின் செல்லாத் தீ வாழ்க்கை', meaning a cruel, unyielding life trapped in a diseased or suffering body. The word 'என்ப' (they say) indicates that this is a recognized truth among the wise. The poem uses the symmetry of bodies, suggesting that destroying another's body leads to suffering in one's own.
